figures.caption: Figure 3 NVCode pipeline. (a) Non-overlapping patches and spectrograms describe each EEG window. (b) Targetspecific encoders learn spatiotemporal and multiscale spectral features under fMRI supervision. (c) A projector combines the features into a neurovascular code. (d) The code conditions joint generation from Gaussian noise through a learned interpolant. (e) Time series and anatomical projections display the regional and global outputs.

Table 1 Eight simultaneous EEG–fMRI datasets span resting-state and task-evoked settings. The source cohorts report 184 participants; after scan-level exclusions, 189 retained scans yield 61,646 paired volumes. Labels follow the source dataset titles, and citations include repository accessions where available.
Table 2 EEG encoder comparison. We fit the same generator architecture separately for each frozen encoder. Higher Avg. R (mean Pearson correlation) and lower marginal CRPS and predictive-mean FC-MAE

Figure 4 EEG encoders on held-out subjects. (a) Pearson R for middle frontal gyrus, cuneus, thalamus, putamen, Heschl’s gyrus, precuneus, and global signal, in axis order. (b) One minus each mean error (CRPS and FC-MAE) from the Inter columns of Table 2. Higher bars correspond to smaller marginal and connectivity errors.
Table 3 Conditional generator comparison. All networks use the same cached EEG codes from seven frozen encoders and the frozen NVCode projector. Each evaluation weights all eight datasets equally.

Figure 5 Generators on held-out subjects. (a) Pearson R for NVCode, DDPM, and CVAE given the same cached EEG codes. Targets follow Figure 4. (b) One minus each mean error (CRPS and FC-MAE) from Table 3, so higher bars indicate lower error. The eight datasets receive equal weight in each held-out-subject summary.

Figure 6 Matched EEG–fMRI evidence for Cuneus. (a, b): Identical EEG inputs in both rows. (c): Real fMRI (black dashed), NVCode (top, red), and EDM (bottom, grey), with correlations. (d): Real, predicted, and absolute-error amplitudes projected onto Cuneus at 54.6 s (purple guides) with a shared color scale.

Table 6 Synthetic fMRI transfers to a classifier trained only on real fMRI. The first row gives real input accuracy; synthetic rows report the change ∆ using predictions from matched EEG epochs. Classifier parameters stay fixed, and Mean weights all eight datasets equally in both the real and synthetic test conditions.
Figure 7 Global signal spectra. Power on log axes for real fMRI and the NVCode and EDM predictive means.

Table 7 Component ablation on held-out subjects. Eight variants test all combinations of regional encoders, joint output, and stochastic interpolation. ✓ and × indicate whether a component is included or excluded.
